A blocked user can no longer message you, and their messages aren’t relayed by your phone. You can unblock them from Settings › Blocked Users.
The report is saved on your phone. If you have a connection, you can forward it to the safety team: every report is reviewed within 24 hours.
AeroChat works wherever there’s no network: in flight, on a cruise, at a festival, in the mountains, or during a blackout. The emergency alert reaches every nearby phone.
Photos from contacts you’ve never scanned in person (group members who arrived via gossip) stay blurred until you tap them.
The simulated travel buddy replies to your messages on this same phone: it’s for trying out (or reviewing) the app without a second phone. It doesn’t use the radio.
Touch and hold a message to block or report the person who wrote it.

AeroChat lets you exchange messages, photos, voice notes, calls, and mini-games between nearby devices over Bluetooth, with no servers and no accounts. The service is provided “as is”: coverage depends on the phones present and isn’t guaranteed.

AeroChat may not be used to harass, threaten, or discriminate, to spread spam or sexually explicit, violent, or illegal content, or to impersonate other people. In the Public Cabin, the rules shown when it is first opened also apply. Anyone who violates these terms can be blocked by other passengers and reported.

Any message you receive can be reported and its author blocked with a single tap. Blocking is immediate and applies on this device: messages from the blocked user are no longer shown or relayed. Reports forwarded by email are reviewed within 24 hours and may lead to abusers being removed from future versions of the app.

The Flight Group Pass is a one-time purchase handled by Google Play, with no automatic renewal. The 72-hour Pass expires at the end of its duration; the Pass Lifetime is permanent. The pass is shared with the members of your groups for the stated duration. Refunds follow Google Play’s policies.
AeroChat is intended for people aged 13 and over. The Public Cabin connects strangers: minors should use it under adult supervision.

The content exchanged is created by users and encrypted end-to-end: it can’t be read or moderated centrally. No liability is accepted for undelivered messages, data loss, or use of the app in violation of the rules of the airline or of the place you’re in.
These terms may be updated with a new version of the app. Continued use after the update constitutes acceptance. For in-app purchases, the Google Play Terms of Service also apply.

AeroChat doesn’t require an email address, phone number, or sign-up. There are no servers receiving your messages: they travel directly between phones over Bluetooth, encrypted end-to-end (X25519, Ed25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305).

Your nickname, color or profile photo, encryption keys, contacts added via QR code, messages, media, games, and reports stay on your phone, in a folder protected by the system. You can delete them by deleting the chats or uninstalling the app.

The travel buddies you chat with see your nickname, color, and profile photo. In the Public Cabin, other passengers see only your nickname and an anonymous technical identifier for your device, which changes if you reinstall the app. Intermediate phones acting as relays see only encrypted packets.

Bluetooth: essential for the mesh network. Camera: QR codes, boarding passes, and photos to send. Microphone: voice notes and calls. Photos: only the images you choose to share or save. Notifications: alerts for incoming messages. Every permission is optional, except Bluetooth.

The app contains no advertising SDKs, third-party analytics, or tracking identifiers. The only communication with the outside world is with Google Play for in-app purchases, which is handled by Google.

If you choose to forward a report by email, the developer receives your email address, the reported user’s nickname and anonymous identifier, and the text of the message. This information is used only to handle the report and is deleted within 90 days.
For privacy questions, write to %1$s. Data controller: the developer listed on the Google Play page.
A message board for passengers within Bluetooth range. To keep it pleasant for everyone, it has a few simple rules.
No insults, harassment, hate, or discrimination. Swear words are censored.
Only your nickname is visible. Anyone who breaks the rules can be blocked and reported by anyone.
Photos, voice notes, and links aren’t allowed on the public board.
Don’t share phone numbers, seat numbers, documents, or other passengers’ details.
The Cabin empties every 12 hours and lives only on the phones on board.
Read the full Terms of Use
No email app installed: write to %1$s.
Translation happens entirely on your phone and nothing leaves the device. The first time, though, each language has to be downloaded (about 30 MB): you need a connection, so do it before your flight.
Some languages aren’t downloaded yet: connect to a network to translate them.
